# syq 0.10.0

This release approves every copy through an enrolled receiver from the
command alone, has server-started downloads read through the source's
enrollment, makes copies faster on long links, network filesystems and
small-file trees, and fixes the findings of a pre-release security review.

## Highlights

- Downloads a server starts with your laptop's approval read through the
  source server's enrolled receiver; the laptop no longer relays the data.
- Copies to and from `@laptop` are approved from the server's command, and a
  bandwidth limit is applied once by the sender.
- `--detach`, `--no-tcp-encryption` and `--follow-dst` work on copies through
  an enrolled receiver, and SSH authorization providers can approve copies
  between two other servers.
- Faster comparison of large files on long links, overlapped publication round
  trips, earlier starts on network filesystems, and shared SSH logins for
  small-file copies.
- Hardening of the restricted receiver: signatures checked before parsing,
  `--no-tcp` enforced on every route, receiver-chosen socket directories, and
  protection of the running copies' sockets.

## Compatibility changes

Install the same syq version on every machine involved in a copy. The first
server-started download from a server enrolls that server's account, as
uploads already did, and the server that starts it must reach the source's SSH
port by itself.

The matching Python package is published after the native release.

See the [0.10.0 changelog](https://github.com/greaber/syq/blob/v0.10.0/CHANGELOG.md)
for the complete behavior changes, compatibility notes and fixes.
